NDT training in North Charleston: how it works for North Charleston employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for North Charleston and the wider Charleston region is delivered live online or onsite at your own plant, hangar, shop or yard. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in North Charleston. An ASNT NDT Level III teaches Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and supports employer examinations and certification. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

North Charleston's industrial base has changed completely in a generation. The Charleston Naval Base and shipyard that once anchored the city closed in the 1990s, and the land along the Cooper River now hosts a commercial shipyard, a new container terminal and industrial tenants. Meanwhile an aerospace cluster grew around Boeing's 787 campus next to the airport and Joint Base Charleston, and automotive, steel and chemical manufacturers settled across Charleston, Berkeley and Dorchester counties. The result is a market where one technician might work on aircraft structure, another on ship hulls, and a third on steel-mill equipment or a port crane, each under different specifications.

Under SNT-TC-1A, all of them are certified the same basic way: by their employer, against a written practice, after training, supervised experience, general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test. We help North Charleston employers run that system and help individuals build the method foundation local employers look for, while being clear that aerospace primes often require NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, and that is not a scheme we train.

Request a North Charleston training quote with the methods, levels, head-count and specifications your customers impose.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in North Charleston

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method. For Lowcountry cohorts we steer the practical toward the product forms local industrial employers inspect: welded structural steel and plate, marine structure, rotating and heavy mill equipment, castings and forgings, and non-magnetic components.

MethodLevelsWhat North Charleston employers use it forPrerequisite
UTI, II, IIIWeld examination on structural steel and heavy fabrications; hull and tank thickness gauging in ship repair; bond and laminate checks in composite manufacturing (under the manufacturer's own scheme)Level I: written-practice entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
PAUTII, IIIEncoded weld examination and corrosion mapping; composite and bond-line scanning in manufacturing environmentsConventional UT Level II first
TOFDII, IIIThick-section weld sizing on heavy industrial and power fabricationsUT Level II
RTI, II, IIIPipe and pressure welds in industrial plants, castings, digital radiography of componentsSouth Carolina radiation-safety requirements for anyone handling sources
MTI, IIStructural welds, crane and port equipment, steel-mill and automotive tooling, ship repairWritten-practice entry rules
PTI, IIAluminium, stainless and titanium parts, machined components, repair welds on non-magnetic materialWritten-practice entry rules
VTI, IIWeld visual on every structural and pressure job, fit-up, corrosion and coating surveysWritten-practice entry rules
ETI, II, IIISurface and near-surface crack detection on aluminium structure and fastener holes, conductivity checks, heat-exchanger tubing in industrial plantsNone; prior UT or PT experience helps

UT. Level I and II courses run from sound physics and transducer selection through calibration, thickness and lamination work, to angle-beam weld examination. North Charleston cohorts get practical exercises on structural and plate welds of the kind produced by local fabricators and ship repairers. Composite inspection is covered as theory because composite aircraft structure is inspected under the manufacturer's own procedures and personnel scheme. Check your readiness with our UT Level 2 practice questions.

PAUT and TOFD. For experienced UT technicians: focal laws, encoded scanning, setup files, corrosion mapping and flaw sizing. Advanced UT is increasingly common in heavy industrial and port work and in automated manufacturing inspection.

RT. Covers exposure technique, image quality indicators, film and digital radiography and interpretation. South Carolina regulates radiation safety separately (see below).

MT and PT. The methods every fabricator, ship repair yard and maintenance department relies on. MT training covers yoke technique, field direction and particle selection; PT covers process control, dwell, cleaning and developer technique, with attention to aluminium and titanium parts where penetrant is standard.

VT. Weld profile gauging, lighting, access, corrosion assessment and clear reporting.

ET. Eddy current courses cover impedance-plane interpretation, surface and bolt-hole probes, conductivity measurement and tubing. Aluminium structure makes surface ET a significant skill in the region's aviation maintenance work, where employers often also require NAS 410 or military qualification.

Level III. Live online preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations, plus procedure writing. See ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in North Charleston, step by step

  1. Written practice. The employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A-based written practice setting training, experience, examination, vision and recertification requirements for each method and level.
  2. Formal training, online, onsite or blended. The training-requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended figures; your written practice may set more.
  3. Supervised experience, logged and signed off by a certified Level II or III.
  4. General examination on principles, equipment and terminology.
  5. Specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment and the codes and customer specifications it works to.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner under one.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity at least annually and colour contrast per the written practice.
  8. Certification signed by the employer.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets (SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years).

More on the employer's responsibilities: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for North Charleston crews

  • Live online. Instructor-led, real-time theory for Level I and II and Level III preparation. Handy for manufacturing employees on rotating shifts. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led team teaches and examines at your plant, yard or shop on your equipment and representative specimens. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory, then an onsite practical and examination block.

Scheduling in the Lowcountry has its own rhythm. Manufacturing plants plan training around production shutdowns, often around the year-end and midsummer holidays. Ship repair follows vessel arrivals. And the Atlantic hurricane season, June through November, can empty a coastal work calendar at short notice and then fill it with post-storm inspections. We plan onsite blocks around your shutdowns and keep online theory flexible. Ask about onsite training for your North Charleston crew.

Practical examinations are always hands-on with real specimens. We do not run remote practicals.

Where NDT technicians work in North Charleston

Aerospace. Boeing South Carolina's 787 campus and its suppliers are the region's largest aerospace employers, and Joint Base Charleston flies and maintains the C-17 fleet of its airlift wings. Aerospace NDT is usually governed by NAS 410 personnel qualification and customer specifications, with Nadcap accreditation for suppliers. That is a different scheme from SNT-TC-1A, and we do not train to it. Technicians who begin with SNT-TC-1A methods in industrial work sometimes move into aerospace later and requalify under the aerospace employer's programme.

Ship repair and the former naval base. Detyens Shipyards operates dry docks on the former Charleston Naval Shipyard, repairing commercial and government vessels. Repair work calls for UT thickness, MT, PT and VT, with ABS or other classification society rules and U.S. Coast Guard requirements on commercial ships and contract-specific requirements on government vessels.

The port. South Carolina Ports' Hugh K. Leatherman Terminal, built on the former navy base, and the North Charleston Terminal handle container traffic with large ship-to-shore cranes and heavy handling equipment that need structural inspection, often MT, UT and VT on crane welds and pins.

Automotive, steel and chemicals. Mercedes-Benz Vans in Ladson, Volvo Cars in Berkeley County, the Nucor steel mill in Berkeley County and chemical and industrial plants in North Charleston and along the Cooper River employ maintenance and quality NDT for tooling, presses, cranes, piping and pressure equipment. Most industrial employers certify under SNT-TC-1A and work to ASME, AWS D1.1 and client specifications.

Power and nuclear. Generating stations in the region bring outage work under ASME codes. Further afield, South Carolina's nuclear plants and the Savannah River Site draw inspectors from the Lowcountry; nuclear UT usually needs performance demonstration qualification on top of SNT-TC-1A training. The Naval Nuclear Power Training Command nearby is a separate military pipeline, but its veterans often move into civilian NDT.

Bridges and highways. The Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge, the Don Holt Bridge on I-526 and ongoing interstate improvement projects need steel inspection, typically to AWS D1.5 for bridge welding and SCDOT specifications.

Radiography licensing in South Carolina. South Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, are licensed and inspected by the Radiation Protection Program of the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services, which took over environmental and radiation regulation from the former SC DHEC. Industrial radiography requirements are set in South Carolina Regulation 61-63, including radiographer training and certification and the licence conditions for field work. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification: most Lowcountry radiographers need both. Out-of-state firms working in South Carolina must follow the state's reciprocity rules.

What employers ask for. Current method certifications and the written practice behind them, training and experience records, a current vision record, TWIC for port facilities, base access for work on Joint Base Charleston, and for aerospace roles the manufacturer's own qualification. For pay information, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources.

Level III services and written practices for North Charleston NDT companies

The Lowcountry's supplier base is young and growing, and many smaller fabricators, machine shops and inspection firms have grown faster than their quality paperwork. When a large customer or a registrar audits, the gaps usually show up in the written practice and the examination records rather than in technician skill. We help with:

  • Written practice development and review matched to the methods you perform and the specifications your customers cite. See written practice development.
  • Examination preparation and grading under ASNT Level III oversight, including specific examinations built around your actual acceptance criteria.
  • Procedure writing aligned to ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 or client specifications, reviewed by a Level III.
  • Audit readiness reviews of certification files before customer or ISO 9001 audits.

Background on the framework is on our SNT-TC-1A guidance page. Book a Level III consultation before your next audit or contract start.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator covers 12 NDT methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. North Charleston trainees heading for industrial and marine work usually get most from the welding workshop; those curious about aviation can explore the hangar. Use it to rehearse setups, scan coverage and interpretation between classes. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who sets course content, oversees examinations and reviews written practices and procedures for employer clients.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in North Charleston

How do I get NDT certified in North Charleston?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training, log supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical examinations and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. We provide training, exam preparation and Level III support online or at the employer's site.

Can I take NDT training online in South Carolina?

Yes, for theory. Practical training and examinations must be hands-on.

Will SNT-TC-1A training get me an aerospace NDT job at Boeing?

Not by itself. Aerospace manufacturers generally qualify NDT personnel under NAS 410 and their own programmes. SNT-TC-1A method training is a solid foundation, but the aerospace employer handles qualification under its scheme, which we do not train.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, based on SNT-TC-1A recommended training and experience hours. Experience is usually the longer part. See the training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in South Carolina?

The company needs a South Carolina radioactive materials licence or machine registration, and radiographers must meet the training and certification requirements in the state's regulations. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

What does NDT training cost in North Charleston?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on method, level, group size, delivery mode and any Level III support. Send your details and we quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by North Charleston employers?

SNT-TC-1A-based certification is widely used by industrial, marine, port and fabrication employers. Aerospace employers usually require NAS 410. Recognition runs through the employer's written practice and records.

Which method should I start with in the Lowcountry?

VT, MT and PT are the most widely used and the usual starting points. Add UT once you have experience; it opens up structural, marine and heavy industrial work.

I am leaving the Navy nuclear programme. Does that count toward NDT certification?

Your technical background helps, but NDT certification requires method-specific training, experience and examinations under an employer's written practice. An employer's Level III decides how much prior training and experience can be credited.

Can you train our maintenance team onsite during a shutdown?

Yes. We plan theory, practical blocks and examinations under your written practice to fit your shutdown window.

Does my certification transfer to a new employer?

Not automatically. The new employer reviews your records and certifies you under its own written practice.

Do you offer Level III preparation?

Yes, live online. See Level III training and our full training catalogue.
